The week in wildlife
Week in wildlife: a hitchhiking crab, a shy wallaby and penguins in little jackets
This week’s best wildlife photographs from around the world
Hitching a ride: a crab inside a barrel jellyfish in the Thracian sea. Photograph: Martina Birrer/Sea Shepherd Global
Pejman Faratin
Fri 4 Sep 2026 08.00 BST
Share
View image in fullscreen
Suits you, sir: Humboldt penguins wear copper bodysuits designed to speed their recovery from surgery at a conservation centre in Coquimbo, Chile. The birds were treated for wounds caused by entanglement in fishing nets: the copper and zinc in the bodysuits help prevent bacterial growth
Photograph: Rodrigo Gutierrez/Reuters
Share
View image in fullscreen
A firefighter rescues an injured animal as the Plaskett fire burns off the California coast, US
Photograph: Ethan Swope/AP
Share
View image in fullscreen
Kākāpō rising:the population of the world’s heaviest parrot,
the much-loved kākāpō
, has surpassed 300 birds for the first time in 75 years, after a record breeding season triggered by the mass fruiting of a native New Zealand tree
Photograph: NZ Department of Conservation
Share
View image in fullscreen
On the hop: Australia’s second smallest wallaby, the shy and nocturnal
nabarlek
, has been detected at two new locations in Western Australia’s vast Kimberley region – a discovery described as like ‘finding a needle in a haystack’
Photograph: Australian Wildlife Conservancy
Share
View image in fullscreen
An octopus curls up inside an artificial reef made from discarded mussel shells near İzmir, Turkey. It is the first resident of the reef, created by entrepreneur Nermin Sena Özger, who sought to provide shelter for marine creatures while diverting waste products from landfill
Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images
Share
View image in fullscreen
Lurking with intent: a large Atlantic ghost crab hides in beach debris, ready to ambush its breakfast on Front Beach, Isle of Palms, South Carolina. Despite their cute and cartoonish appearance, ghost crabs are fast, aggressive predators that prey on young sea turtles and shorebird hatchlings
Photograph: Richard Ellis/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock
Share
View image in fullscreen
A Phayre’s leaf monkey – also known as a spectacled monkey because of the rings around its eyes – peers down from a tree in Lawachara national park in eastern Bangladesh. The species has faced a significant decline due to deforestation, habitat fragmentation, road construction and other threats to its forest habitat
Photograph: NurPhoto/Getty Images
Share
View image in fullscreen
Wardens with Kenya Wildlife Services remove netting from a Nile crocodile they caught in Lake Baringo. Crocodiles there are being translocated to help reduce cases of human-wildlife conflict around Marigat, a fast-growing town nearby. Lake Baringo and other lakes in Kenya’s Rift valley have risen to levels not seen in at least half a century, with scientists attributing the surge to extreme rainfall linked to climate change
Photograph: Tony Karumba/AFP/Getty Images
Share
View image in fullscreen
All ears: this injured jerboa was found in the wild by a shepherd, who brought it to his home for treatment in Kayseri, Turkey
Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

View image in fullscreen
A forest official stands guard as a one-horned rhinoceros crosses the road to move towards the Pobitora wildlife sanctuary on the outskirts of Guwahati, eastern India
Photograph: Anupam Nath/AP
Share
View image in fullscreen
Hitching a ride: a photographer onboard a Sea Shepherd Conservation Society ship captured this picture of a crab hitchhiking inside a barrel jellyfish in the Thracian sea, northern Greece
Photograph: Martina Birrer/Sea Shepherd Global

View image in fullscreen
Veterinarians treat an orangutang named Sampurna during a rescue operation at a palm oil plantation near an area affected by wildfires, in Kuala Satong village, West Kalimantan, Indonesia
Photograph: Willy Kurniawan/Reuters

Photograph: Dogan Evsan/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

Photograph: Colorado Parks and Wildlife /Reuters
